Subject: Third-party residency exception & telemetry proof

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the quick intro earlier. As part of our procurement security review for the Redwood Private deployment, SecOps needs two things clarified before we can proceed to legal: a) a signed list of all subprocessors that may handle patient-related inference data and their residency (country/region) and b) an evidence package that demonstrates telemetry retention, what data is sent to Redwood control plane vs. customer VPC, and the key custody model (specifically whether RSA/HSM keys ever leave the customer KMS boundary).

Can you provide a short CSV roster and a compact evidence bundle (SOC2 scope extract, CAIQ answers for hosting/residency, and a telemetry retention matrix)? If any subprocessors have exceptional residency (e.g., transient analytics in a different region) please flag those and note compensating controls.

Best,
Alice Monroe
Senior Security Engineer
HealthBridge Medical

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@healthbridge.com>
Date: 2026-08-01 09:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Third-party residency exception & telemetry proof

Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. I can get an initial roster and a telemetry matrix over; however, I will need to loop in our SRE lead (Logan) and our compliance engineer (Ben) for the key custody specifics. Quick notes up front:

- Redwood Private by default keeps inference data inside the customer VPC and control plane interactions are metadata-only; we document what metadata flows to the control plane.
- Telemetry types: health/metrics, anonymized aggregate usage, error traces; retention depends on customer plan (hosted defaults 90 days telemetry, Dedicated/Private can be configured up to 365 days).
- Key model: Private customers commonly bring their own KMS (customer-managed keys); ephemeral session keys for KV cache are rotated inside host boundary and never escrowed by Redwood unless explicitly requested in a contractual addendum.

I will assemble: subprocessor_roster_20260801.csv, telemetry_retention_matrix.pdf, and a short key_escrow_playbook.md that explains options (BYOK, HSM handoff, escrow for recovery).

ETA: initial bundle by Monday EOD (2026-08-03). If HealthBridge needs anything earlier we can prioritize.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Security Outreach, Redwood Inference

From: logan_wright@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Third-party residency exception & telemetry proof

Ben / Olga —

Telemetry & control-plane notes to include in the matrix:
- Control-plane metadata (request routing, model selection logs) is stored in our control-plane database replicated in us-west-2 and in a dedicated EU region for customers who elect EU residency. For Redwood Private deployments the control-plane can be configured to run in-customer-region or use private connectivity (no telemetry leaves the VPC unless customer enables).
- Telemetry buckets: metrics (aggregated), traces (errors), model-usage (token counts), storing as pseudonymized IDs. Default retention: Hosted 90 days, Dedicated 180 days, Private configurable 0-365 (customer choice).
- KV cache: for Private we recommend local cache — no data leaves VPC. For Hosted we use CacheWorks in us-west-2; cache keys are ephemeral and rotated every 8 hours.
- Key custody: BYOK via customer KMS is standard for Private customers; we only hold wrapped recovery keys in an escrow workflow when explicitly permitted by contract. Escrow requires HSM-backed encryption and dual-operator approvals.

I'll prepare a short one-page matrix (telemetry_retention_matrix.pdf) and clarify which subprocessors may process telemetry in EU for transient analytics.

Thanks,
Logan
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the initial evidence bundle per your request:

- Attachment: subprocessor_roster_20260801.csv (CSV, 52KB) — columns: vendor_name, role, residency, processing_scope, compensating_controls
- Attachment: telemetry_retention_matrix.pdf (PDF, 18KB) — summarizes buckets, default retention, and configuration knobs for Private/Dedicated/Hosted
- Attachment: key_escrow_playbook.md (MD, 6KB) — outlines BYOK, HSM escrow process, operator approvals, and example contract language for escrow exceptions
- Drive link with raw artifacts and SOC2 extracts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleEvidence

Top-level clarifications:
- For Redwood Private deployments (the model HealthBridge is evaluating) control-plane telemetry can be kept out of customer VPCs or hosted in-customer-region via private connectivity; no inference content leaves the customer network unless explicitly configured.
- Transient analytics (EdgeMetrics Inc.) is limited to aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry and is flagged in the roster column "compensating_controls" with contractual restrictions and DPA clauses.
- Key custody: BYOK + HSM-backed escrow only on request; default is customer-managed KMS with no Redwood access to unwrapped keys.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute SecOps walk-through early next week to review the matrix and the SOC2 snippets. Please let me know an available slot and whether you need any additional artifacts (CAIQ answers, penetration test summary, or DocuSign DPA template).

Best,
